question: Which court in the subordinate judiciary has unlimited pecuniary jurisdiction in civil cases? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Small Causes Court
Nyaya Panchayat
Court of Munsiff
Judge of District Court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Judge of District Court

Explanation:
In the subordinate judiciary, the Judge of District Court has unlimited pecuniary jurisdiction in civil cases. This court is the highest civil court at the district level and can entertain suits of any value. In contrast, the Small Causes Court has limited jurisdiction (usually up to 5,000 rupees). The Court of Munsiff also has limited jurisdiction (up to a few lakh rupees). The Nyaya Panchayat is a village-level court with jurisdiction over small civil and criminal cases. Hence, only the District Judge's court has unlimited pecuniary jurisdiction.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Pecuniary jurisdiction of District Judge → Unlimited
☛ Maximum pecuniary limit of Small Causes Court → 5,000 rupees
☛ Jurisdiction of Munsiff Court → Limited (up to a few lakhs)
☛ Level of Nyaya Panchayat → Village level
☛ Highest subordinate civil court → District Court
question_hi: ​अधीन न्यायपालिका में किस न्यायालय को दीवानी मामलों में असीमित आर्थिक अधिकारिता प्राप्त है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)

न्याय पंचायत
मुनसिफ का न्यायालय

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है जिला न्यायालय का न्यायाधीश

Explanation:
अधीन न्यायपालिका में दीवानी मामलों में असीमित आर्थिक अधिकारिता जिला न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश को प्राप्त है। यह अदालत सबसे उच्च स्तर की दीवानी अदालत है जो जिला स्तर पर कार्य करती है। इसके अंतर्गत किसी भी मूल्य के दीवानी मुकदमे दायर किए जा सकते हैं। वहीं, लघु वाद न्यायालय सीमित आर्थिक अधिकारिता (आमतौर पर 5,000 रुपये तक) रखता है। मुनसिफ का न्यायालय भी सीमित अधिकारिता (कुछ लाख रुपये तक) रखता है। न्याय पंचायत ग्राम स्तर की अदालत है जिसके पास छोटे दीवानी और फौजदारी मामलों की अधिकारिता होती है। इस प्रकार, असीमित आर्थिक अधिकारिता केवल जिला न्यायाधीश के न्यायालय को प्राप्त है।

question: Who among the following is responsible for implementing decisions made by a Municipal Corporation’s council and standing committees in India?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Chairman
Municipal Commissioner
Standing Committee Head
Deputy Mayor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Municipal Commissioner

Explanation:
In India's Municipal Corporation system, the Municipal Commissioner is the chief executive officer responsible for implementing decisions made by the corporation's council and standing committees. The Municipal Commissioner is a senior administrative officer, typically from the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) or state civil service, appointed by the state government. This role involves managing daily operations, preparing budgets, overseeing various departments, and executing policies approved by the council. In contrast, the Mayor serves as the ceremonial head, while standing committees deliberate on policy matters. The Commissioner can attend council meetings but does not have voting rights. This structure ensures a separation between deliberative functions (council and committees) and executive functions (Commissioner), making the Commissioner the key implementing authority.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who is the executive head of a Municipal Corporation? → Municipal Commissioner
☛ From which service is the Municipal Commissioner usually appointed? → IAS or state civil service
☛ Who is the ceremonial head of a Municipal Corporation? → Mayor
☛ Who implements decisions of standing committees? → Municipal Commissioner
☛ Who appoints the Municipal Commissioner? → State Government
question_hi: भारत में, नगर निगम की परिषद और स्थायी समितियों द्वारा लिएगए निर्णयों को लागू करने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन उत्तरदायी है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)

नगर आयुक्त

Solution: सही उत्तर है नगर आयुक्त

Explanation:

question: The Recorder’s Court was later replaced by the ______. (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Supreme Court
High Courts
Privy Council
Sessions Courts
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Supreme Court

Explanation:
The Recorder's Court was later replaced by the Supreme Court. The Recorder's Court was a judicial system established during the British period in presidency towns like Madras, Bombay, and Calcutta. Its primary function was to hear criminal cases. Later, as part of the reform of the Indian judicial system, it was transformed into the Supreme Court under the Regulating Act of 1773 and the Charter Act of 1793. This change was made to strengthen judicial independence and the rule of law. The Supreme Court was the highest court in each presidency and eventually paved the way for the modern judiciary.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Where was the Recorder's Court first established? → Madras
☛ What replaced the Recorder's Court? → Supreme Court
☛ What type of cases did the Recorder's Court handle? → Criminal cases
☛ Which act established the Supreme Court? → Regulating Act of 1773
☛ In which cities was the Recorder's Court located? → Madras, Bombay, Calcutta

Explanation:
उत्तरकाल में रिकॉर्डर कोर्ट का स्थान सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने लिया। रिकॉर्डर कोर्ट एक ब्रिटिश कालीन न्यायिक प्रणाली थी, जो मद्रास, बॉम्बे और कलकत्ता जैसे प्रेसीडेंसी शहरों में स्थापित की गई थी। इसका मुख्य कार्य आपराधिक मामलों की सुनवाई करना था। बाद में, भारतीय न्याय प्रणाली के सुधार के तहत इसे 1773 के रेग्युलेटिंग एक्ट और 1793 के चार्टर एक्ट के माध्यम से सर्वोच्च न्यायालय (सुप्रीम कोर्ट) में बदल दिया गया। यह परिवर्तन न्यायिक स्वतंत्रता और कानून के शासन को मजबूत करने के लिए किया गया था।

question: In some cases, the Prime Minister of India assigns an independent charge of a portfolio to a Minister of State. This implies that the Minister of State: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: is demoted in responsibilities
loses the title of Minister of State
serves jointly with a Cabinet Minister to share and perform responsibilities of the assigned portfolio
functions as if in Cabinet rank with full independent responsibility for that portfolio
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is functions as if in Cabinet rank with full independent responsibility for that portfolio

Explanation:
When the Prime Minister assigns independent charge of a portfolio to a Minister of State, that minister becomes the sole head of that department and functions akin to a Cabinet Minister. In such a role, the Minister of State does not work under any Cabinet Minister but reports directly to the Prime Minister. The minister exercises full powers and responsibilities of that portfolio independently, though the official title remains Minister of State. This arrangement allows the minister to operate with Cabinet rank status, including attending Cabinet meetings when invited, and having full decision-making authority for the assigned ministry.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What rank is given to a Minister of State with independent charge? → Cabinet rank
☛ To whom does a Minister of State with independent charge report? → Prime Minister
☛ Can a Minister of State with independent charge attend Cabinet meetings? → Yes, if invited
☛ How many types of ministers are there in the Union Council of Ministers? → Three: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State (Independent Charge), Ministers of State
☛ A Minister of State with independent charge enjoys powers equivalent to which minister? → Cabinet Minister

question: Which type of legislative bills must be introduced in the Lok Sabha only after obtaining the prior approval of the President of India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Private Bills
Ordinary Bills
Public Bills
Money Bills
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Money Bills

Explanation:
According to Article 117 of the Indian Constitution, Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha with the prior recommendation of the President of India. A Money Bill deals with matters such as the imposition, abolition, alteration, or regulation of taxes; the borrowing of money; the custody of the Consolidated Fund; or the appropriation of money from the Consolidated Fund. The requirement for presidential approval ensures that the government controls financial legislation. Money Bills are introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations but cannot reject them. The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days, and the Lok Sabha may accept or reject its recommendations. The President's assent is final.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article 117 → Relates to President's recommendation for Money Bills
☛ Money Bill definition → Given in Article 110 of the Constitution
☛ Who introduces a Money Bill → Only a minister in the Lok Sabha
☛ Rajya Sabha's role → Can recommend changes but cannot reject Money Bill
☛ Finance Bill vs Money Bill → Finance Bill often requires President's recommendation but is not the same
question_hi: किस प्रकार के विधायी विधेयक लोकसभा में केवल भारत के राष्ट्रपति की पूर्व स्वीकृति प्राप्त करने के बाद ही पेश किए जा सकते हैं? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: निजी विधेयक
साधारण विधेयक
सार्वजनिक विधेयक
धन विधेयक
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है धन विधेयक

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 117 के अनुसार, धन विधेयक को लोकसभा में केवल राष्ट्रपति की पूर्व अनुशंसा से ही पेश किया जा सकता है। धन विधेयक वह विधेयक है जो करों के लगाने, उठाने, संग्रह या विनियोग, भारत की संचित निधि से धन की निकासी आदि से संबंधित होता है। राष्ट्रपति की अनुशंसा आवश्यक है क्योंकि यह सरकार के वित्तीय मामलों से जुड़ा होता है। धन विधेयक केवल लोकसभा में पेश किया जाता है, राज्यसभा इसे केवल अनुशंसा कर सकती है, लेकिन इसे रोक नहीं सकती। इसके अलावा, राज्यसभा द्वारा सिफारिशों को लोकसभा द्वारा अस्वीकार किया जा सकता है। धन विधेयक पर राष्ट्रपति की सहमति अनिवार्य है।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

question: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of tribal areas in which region? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: North-East India
Western Ghats
Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Central India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is North-East India

Explanation:
The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of tribal areas in North-East India. It provides special provisions for the tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Under this schedule, District Councils and Regional Councils are formed, which have the power to make laws on land, forests, agriculture, social customs, etc. This schedule ensures the protection of tribal culture and rights while promoting development. It is connected with Article 244(2) and Article 275(1) of the Constitution. In non-North-Eastern regions, tribal administration comes under the Fifth Schedule.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which states are covered under the Sixth Schedule? → Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
☛ Bodies formed under the Sixth Schedule? → District Councils and Regional Councils
☛ Which areas are covered under the Fifth Schedule? → Tribal areas except North-East
☛ Constitutional basis of the Sixth Schedule? → Article 244(2) and 275(1)
☛ Which amendment introduced Sixth Schedule in Mizoram and Tripura? → 49th Amendment, 1984

question: Reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India related to the accounts of a state shall be submitted to whom among the following? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Prime Minister of India
President of India
Chief Minister of the concerned state
Governor of the concerned state
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor of the concerned state

Explanation:
According to Article 151 of the Constitution of India, the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) relating to the accounts of a state are submitted to the Governor of that state. The Governor then causes them to be laid before the state legislature. This provision ensures financial accountability within the federal structure. The CAG is an independent constitutional authority responsible for auditing public finances. For the Union, the reports are submitted to the President. At the state level, the Governor acts as the representative of the central government and receives these reports. Neither the Chief Minister nor the Prime Minister receives these reports directly. The Governor's role is crucial in maintaining transparency and oversight of state expenditures.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states about the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 148
Article 147

Article 146
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 148

Explanation:
Article 148 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, oath, and conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG). The CAG is appointed by the President and takes an oath before the President before assuming office. This provision falls under Part V of the Constitution. question: Which two articles of the Constitution of India most clearly express the power of judicial review? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Article 44 and Article 152
Article 21 and Article 446
Article 17 and Article 143
Article 32 and Article 226
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 32 and Article 226

Explanation:
Judicial review refers to the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of laws or executive orders and declare them void if they violate the Constitution. In the Indian Constitution, Article 32 and Article 226 most clearly embody the power of judicial review. Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights, while Article 226 confers similar power on the High Courts. These articles are part of the 'Right to Constitutional Remedies' and enable the judiciary to review legislative and executive actions. They are considered the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, as they ensure that fundamental rights are not violated.

question: Which constitutional amendment, known as 'mini constitution', gave effect to the recommendations of Swaran Singh Committee?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: 43rd constitutional amendment
44th constitutional amendment
42nd constitutional amendment
41St constitutional amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd constitutional amendment

Explanation:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) is known as the 'mini constitution'. It gave effect to the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. It introduced the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity in the Preamble. It added Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A) and curtailed judicial review. It made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers, expanded the amending power under Article 368, and gave precedence to Directive Principles (Part IV) over Fundamental Rights (Part III). This amendment was controversial, and many of its provisions were later repealed by the 43rd and 44th amendments.

☛ Based on Swaran Singh Committee recommendations → 42nd Amendment
☛ Words added to Preamble → Socialist, Secular, Integrity

☛ Gave precedence to DPSP over Fundamental Rights → 42nd Amendment

लोकसभा में सीटों का वितरण जनसंख्या के आधार पर किया गया है। वर्तमान में उत्तर प्रदेश में 80 लोकसभा सीटें हैं, जो देश में सबसे अधिक है। महाराष्ट्र में 48, गुजरात में 26, और राजस्थान में 25 सीटें हैं। उत्तर प्रदेश की सबसे अधिक सीटें इसकी विशाल जनसंख्या के कारण हैं, जो भारत में सबसे बड़ी है। लोकसभा सीटों का वितरण संविधान के अनुसार समय-समय पर समायोजित किया जाता है। अंतिम परिसीमन 2008 में हुआ था।
